title: Orchestrated parity migration preview
summary: Intro and high-level demo showing how to map OpenAI/Anthropic/Together endpoints to the Redwood API, console walk-through for routing + Optimize suggestions, and a concrete benchmark and pilot plan. Customer raised questions on tokenization differences, private deployment latency, and SOC2/KMS. Action items agreed for parity spreadsheet, benchmark, and security package.
topics: parity mapping for generation and chat endpoints
model name/version equivalence and tokenization differences
console tour: routing, rollouts, and Optimize recommendations
benchmark plan: latency, cost, and quality metrics
next_steps: Maya to send parity mapping spreadsheet and initial cost model by 2027-01-07
Ravi to run side-by-side latency and token-cost benchmark on Atlas sample workload and share raw results by 2027-01-12
Olivia to provide security package (SOC2 summary, KMS integration notes) and draft SSO flow by 2027-01-10
Schedule pilot kickoff call (2-3 week initial pilot) - target week of 2027-01-18

Ravi Patel: Run 3-config perf runs (streaming vs non-streaming) with Atlas prompt set; include KV cache on/off (due 2027-01-12)

meeting_header: Date: 2027-01-05 15:00 UTC; Duration: 62m; Recording: yes; Location: Zoom; Redwood AE+SE; Customer (Atlas Bioinformatics)
transcript: 00:00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll-call?
00:00:08 Eleanor Price: Hi, Eleanor here - CTO. We have Samir, Jenna and Marco on our side too.

00:00:15 Maya Chen: Great. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Ravi and Olivia here on the product/SE side. We're going to walk through a parity mapping demo for switching from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to the Redwood API, then show the Console + Optimize suggestions, and finish with a pilot plan.
00:00:35 Marco D'Angelo: Quick ask up front — we need minimal changes to our runtime and cost estimates. Also, low-latency for our interactive QA UI is critical.
00:00:45 Ravi Patel: Totally. We'll focus on a route-for-route mapping and highlight tokenization and streaming differences — those are often the subtle bits.
00:00:54 Samir Khan: Also curious about function-calling parity — we use structured responses a lot.

00:01:02 Olivia Martinez: We'll demo the function/tool calling compatibility and how Redwood maps schema and streaming responses. Sometimes function names or fields get renamed in transcripts; we'll show the recommended adapter layer.

00:01:18 Maya Chen: Alright starting the screen. First slide is a simple mapping table — OpenAI chat/completions, Anthropic's Claude-style calls, Together — mapped to Redwood model ids and recommended params.
00:01:35 Maya Chen: Note: we recommend warm KV cache and streaming enabled for UI paths to keep tail latency low — we'll show numbers later.
00:01:50 Jenna Lee: Quick clarification: when you say KV cache, do you mean prefix caching of past conversation tokens or something else?
00:01:58 Ravi Patel: Prefix/KV cache — the key-value cache for transformer states. In Redwood we expose tunable TTLs and cache scopes per route, that helps reduce repeated prefix cost.
00:02:12 Eleanor Price: How close is tokenization to OpenAI? We saw a few tokens difference on our counters when testing other runtimes.

00:02:20 Ravi Patel: Good question. Redwood uses the same BPE/byte-level tokenizers for the model families we host, but small differences can arise when you mix model families. We include a tokenizer-check step in the parity spreadsheet so you can compare token counts on your real prompts.
00:02:35 Marco D'Angelo: Okay, show us the actual request/response example — we want to see how little code changes are needed.

00:02:43 Maya Chen: Switching to a live API example. Here's a typical OpenAI chat call and the equivalent Redwood POST to /v1/chat/completions. The fields map 1:1 for messages, max_tokens, temperature. For function-calling we support a 'tools' object and the streamed deltas include tool invocation events.
00:03:05 Samir Khan: Any gotchas on streaming protocol? We use SSE in-house now.

00:03:11 Ravi Patel: We support server-sent events and chunked HTTP streaming. One subtlety: our streaming chunks include an explicit chunk-type header for function events so your client can differentiate partial text vs tool-json. Helps avoid double-parsing.
00:03:30 Jenna Lee: Does streaming change pricing?
00:03:34 Olivia Martinez: Pricing is token-based; streaming doesn't change per-token billing. However, enabling KV cache and batching will reduce consumed tokens and throughput costs.
00:03:44 Eleanor Price: How about model variants — do you do quantized variants for cost? We run a mix of high-quality and lower-cost routes.

00:03:51 Ravi Patel: Yes, we offer quantized variants and recommend tiered routing policies. You can route lower cost quantized models for background tasks and keep high-precision for user-facing paths. The Console has an A/B rollout and fallback policy UI.
00:04:06 Maya Chen: Let's jump to the Console. Olivia, can you guide them through routing and Optimize suggestions?

00:04:11 Olivia Martinez: Sure. Pulling up the per-route dashboard — here you can see latency percentiles, token consumption, and Optimize's suggestions. For this demo I toggled a simulated workload. Notice Optimize recommends batching for high-throughput endpoints and KV cache for chat-heavy flows.
00:04:32 Marco D'Angelo: That batching suggestion — how invasive is it in our client logic?

00:04:37 Ravi Patel: Usually none in the client if you use Redwood's SDK. For stateless HTTP requests we offer a batching client that assembles several short prompts into one batch and splits responses. If you're on an in-house connector, it's a small shim.
00:04:50 Samir Khan: About private deployments — we need VPC, KMS, and audit logs. Does Redwood's private package support HSM-backed keys?

00:04:59 Olivia Martinez: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS and HSMs, and we expose audit logs and request-level traces. Our private control plane can sit in your VPC or be deployed on-prem depending on compliance needs.
00:05:14 Jenna Lee: Any perf delta for on-prem vs hosted? We're worried about GPU allocation and autoscaling behaviors.

00:05:22 Ravi Patel: On private, perf is determined by your hardware and how you size the cluster. Redwood's runtime includes GPU-optimized kernels, but you will need to size for peak concurrency. For Dedicated (hosted reserved capacity), we provide SLO-backed latency targets and autoscaling policies.
00:05:35 Eleanor Price: Security-wise we need SOC2 plus a data residency note — can you share certs?
00:05:41 Olivia Martinez: Absolutely. I'll attach the SOC2 summary and a one-page KMS integration guide in the security package.

00:05:48 Maya Chen: Ok back to parity: here's the mapping sheet — model ids, recommended temperature, stop sequences, and function schema differences. Important: Together uses a slightly different priming pattern; we recommend a small prompt adapter that normalizes system prompts to Redwood's preferred framing.
00:06:08 Samir Khan: Any automatic adapters or do we write that ourselves?
00:06:12 Ravi Patel: We provide small reference adapters in Node/Python as part of the onboarding repo — they're 20–50 lines typically.
00:06:20 Marco D'Angelo: We measure hallucination and QA accuracy. How do you validate quality parity?

00:06:25 Olivia Martinez: We recommend a two-step: automated evals on your seed prompts (ROC curves, F1 for extraction tasks) and a small human review for edge cases. Redwood's Optimize can track regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
00:06:38 Samir Khan: For benchmarking, we need to reproduce our 95th percentile latency under 300ms on the UI path. Is that realistic on your Hosted plan?

00:06:45 Ravi Patel: Yes for short contexts and streaming enabled. We'll benchmark with and without KV cache and show p50/p95/p99 figures. We'll also show token-cost delta so you can compare unit economics.

00:06:58 Maya Chen: Now a short live demo making an API call through Redwood vs OpenAI. I'll show the payload and the response timing. Keep in mind network variances — we'll run the formal perf tests offline.

00:07:12 (screen share: terminal) Ravi Patel: Initiating 1 request with streaming. 00:07:20 (terminal) Response begins streaming — you can see chunk-type 'text' then chunk-type 'tool' when function is invoked.
00:07:36 Samir Khan: That chunk-type header is helpful. We had to do heuristics previously and it caused flakiness.

00:07:42 Maya Chen: Moving to the Optimize console recommendations — here's a suggestion to flip on a lightweight quantized variant for nightly batch jobs, and to use dedicated pools for the UI route.
00:07:54 Jenna Lee: If we use dedicated pools for UI, can those pools burst to hosted? We don't want to lose availability during traffic spikes.

00:08:01 Olivia Martinez: Yes, there's a burst policy option. You can reserve capacity and allow overflow to the shared fleet with cost controls. We also configure fallback model variants to preserve availability.
00:08:12 Marco D'Angelo: Pricing question — how do you handle multi-model costs when we split traffic?

00:08:17 Maya Chen: Our pricing model gives per-token rates per model variant, and the Console breaks down token spend by route and model. We'll include a preliminary cost model for your expected traffic.
00:08:28 Samir Khan: On tokenization again — do you provide offline tokenizers so we can pre-calc counts before calls?
00:08:34 Ravi Patel: Yes, we include tokenizer binaries and a small CLI so you can run token counts locally. That helps with quota planning and pre-tokenizing long docs for embeddings or chunking.
00:08:45 Eleanor Price: Can you run a small proof-of-concept against our data — we'll provide prompt seeds and a sample trace?

00:08:51 Maya Chen: Yes, that's the pilot plan: 2–3 weeks, side-by-side perf and quality runs, and a short integration to validate function-calling and streaming. We'll scope the pilot after we get your seed prompts and traces.
00:09:03 (a few minutes of Q&A, some brief silence as they load a doc)
00:14:50 Jenna Lee: One more infra question — network egress and VPC endpoints. If we run private deployment in our VPC, what's the egress profile?

00:14:58 Olivia Martinez: For VPC-hosted control plane, egress is customer-controlled. For hosted dedicated, we recommend using regional endpoints and setting up our VPC peering. We'll send a diagram.
00:15:10 Marco D'Angelo: Any compatibility issues with our existing observability? We use Honeycomb and internal tracing.
00:15:17 Ravi Patel: We emit traces and expose hooks; we can push spans to Honeycomb or export OTLP. We'll add a short example in the integration repo.
00:15:30 (Maya flips to pilot timeline slide)

00:15:35 Maya Chen: Proposed pilot: week 1 integrate SDK + parity adapter and run smoke tests. Week 2 run automated benchmarks (latency, cost, quality). Week 3 iterate and sign-off or expand. We'll provide a pilot checklist.
00:15:48 Eleanor Price: Sounds good. Budget-wise, what's an estimate for a 3-week pilot?
00:15:54 Maya Chen: We'll send a pilot quote — low-cost sandbox credits plus optional dedicated short-term capacity if you want SLO-backed numbers. I'll include pricing bands in the follow-up.
00:16:05 Samir Khan: Regarding model variance — Together had a slightly different EOS handling and we saw truncated responses. Does Redwood normalize that?
00:16:14 Ravi Patel: We normalize and recommend a post-processor for a small set of edge rules. The adapter repo has hooks for EOS fixes and stop-sequence enforcement.
00:16:26 Marco D'Angelo: Who would be our main SE during the pilot?
00:16:29 Maya Chen: Ravi will be the technical lead and Olivia will support the Console/Optimize pieces.
00:16:34 Olivia Martinez: We'll be on the pilot calls and run the shared dashboards with you.
00:16:40 (customers ask about legal and procurement timeline)
00:16:48 Eleanor Price: Our procurement needs a DPA and standard terms; can you share a sample?
00:16:53 Maya Chen: Yes, legal can share a DPA and standard enterprise contract. I'll ask our legal to send the initial package after this call.
00:16:59 Jenna Lee: Any concerns about data residency for EU users? We have EU patient traces in some subsets.
00:17:06 Olivia Martinez: We have region-aware routing and private deployment options. For EU-residency, we can pin to regional hosts and show audit logs that data didn't egress.
00:17:16 (longer section where Ravi walks through a sample parity spreadsheet live; customers ask clarifying questions about parameter names)
00:25:42 Samir Khan: There's a line here about 'temperature mapping' where Anthropic's safety priming changed effective temperature — is that documented?
00:25:49 Ravi Patel: Yes, we add a recommended delta to temperature when mapping from Anthropic models because the prompting system differences alter entropy. It's in the notes column.
00:26:02 Marco D'Angelo: We also need to log model version pins for reproducibility. How does Redwood handle version pinning and rollbacks?

00:26:09 Olivia Martinez: You can pin a model version per route and create rollouts: canary -> gradual -> full. Rollbacks are one-click in Console and you can set auto-fallback to previous stable variant.
00:26:22 Eleanor Price: For our audit trails, do we get per-request metadata like user-id, trace-id?
00:26:28 Ravi Patel: Yes, we accept metadata headers and surface them in traces and logs. We also support redaction rules for PII.
00:26:38 Maya Chen: Ok quick demo of a failure scenario and graceful degradation: we simulate a spike and show routing to a lower-cost quantized fallback.
00:26:50 (demo run) 00:26:58 Olivia Martinez: See here, requests hit the primary pool and then overflow to the fallback; Console highlights the fallback traffic.
00:27:08 Marco D'Angelo: That would be helpful for our incident runbooks.
00:27:12 Maya Chen: Final Qs before we wrap?
00:27:15 Jenna Lee: One more on billing: is there a minimum for dedicated pools?
00:27:19 Maya Chen: Yes dedicated has reserve minimums; we'll include example commit tiers in our pricing doc.
00:27:26 Eleanor Price: Okay great. Let's confirm next steps — you'll send parity sheet, security docs, and we'll provide prompt seeds.
00:27:34 Maya Chen: Correct. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff. Thanks everyone, we'll send the materials after the call.
00:27:41 (call wraps; informal chatter and goodbyes)
00:28:00 Post-call notes: Customer to share 500–1k seed prompts and traces. Redwood to prepare sandbox credentials and run initial perf tests. We'll coordinate on the pilot kickoff date.

00:28:32 Transcription quirks: sometimes 'KV cache' appears as 'K V cash' and 'VPC' transcribed as 'V P C P' in the raw caption; proper nouns like 'TogetherAI' were sometimes 'Together I' in auto transcript.
